A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MuLoCo study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original language-model training experiments, communication and compression studies, scaling analyses, system measurements, and downstream benchmark results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and adds efficiency analyses derived from the reported training runs.

M1.justification: The Muon inner updates, pseudogradient averaging, Nesterov outer optimizer, compression, and error feedback remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 explicitly label the existing local step counter t without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Nemotron-CC pretraining, the same downstream benchmarks, and the same communication, compression, streaming, and bandwidth scenarios. The added efficiency analyses introduce no new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: DiLoCo, DP AdamW, and DP Muon remain the evaluated comparators in corresponding experiments. The additional related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 7.2 adds training-time efficiency at fixed loss, replacing the main figure's fixed-time loss comparison while retaining that comparison in the appendix. Appendix C.2 adds compute efficiency at optimal batch size. Training settings and hyperparameter sweeps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The revised efficiency analysis distinguishes compute savings from the advantage of larger critical batch sizes, with an additional compute-efficiency analysis in Appendix C.2. Existing compression, synchronization, streaming, and pseudogradient analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Scaling-law initialization restarts, validation-loss smoothing, and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. V3 adds no training-seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 newly reports an approximately 4.5-fold training-time efficiency ratio at fixed loss (Figure 13) and approximately 1.35-fold compute efficiency (Figure 18). These are derived scaling-law findings, not improved training outcomes between versions. Existing numerical tables and the earlier fixed-time performance curve are retained.

T1.justification: V3 adds the fixed-loss efficiency definition and its decomposition into compute savings and parallelism advantage (Equation 6). The pseudogradient propositions and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Section 7.2 revises the critical-batch inequality to use losses, but its 0.01 multiplier remains inconsistent with Figure 1's 1.01 criterion.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the core contributions: Muon as DiLoCo's inner optimizer, improved worker scaling, larger critical batch sizes, and the single-worker performance–time advantage. The new efficiency estimates elaborate these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 4 explicitly characterizes the proposed link between pseudogradient structure and performance as speculative. Section 8 completes the unfinished limitations paragraph, adding untested outer optimizers and the absence of a convergence proof. Section 7.2 also distinguishes fixed-loss efficiency from FLOP-matched comparisons.

D1.justification: Section 5 removes the blanket statement that DP baselines share the inner optimizers' hyperparameter choices, while Appendix E retains the same detailed settings. Algorithms 1–2 explicitly identify t as the local step counter. These are limited documentation refinements; hardware, implementations, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 adds Cheng and Glasgow, MT-DAO, DES-LOC, and LORDO, discussing optimizer-state communication and its convergence, performance, and communication tradeoffs. The broader research positioning remains unchanged; publication and author-name updates are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites the method motivation and efficiency discussion, completes the limitations paragraph, and makes wording and bibliographic corrections. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 13(a) is replaced by a fixed-loss efficiency plot. Its earlier curve moves to Figure 18(b), alongside a new compute-efficiency panel. Figure 1(b)'s normalization label is clarified, and several displays shift position; existing tables and other plots are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 more clearly distinguishes compute savings, fixed-loss time savings, and FLOP-matched performance. Its explicit mechanism caveats and completed limitations also improve interpretation. These are limited, evidence-supported gains; the critical-batch inequality remains inconsistent with Figure 1, and the underlying experimental evidence is unchanged.
